sara.security: Heads-up: Received a privacy request from a customer asking us to delete all embeddings for guest email guest123@example.com. Found hits in prod embeddings index and in nightly S3 snapshots encrypted with kms-prod-redwood. Any constraints we should expect?

jose.privacy: Do we have proof of requester identity? Need verification before action. Also check if there's any legal hold flag for that org.

sara.security: Verified via support ticket + email confirmation, already logged. No existing legal hold in our tracker (legal-team please confirm).

li.engineering: On the embeddings side: we index vectors with metadata.user_email and metadata.user_id. Quick query I ran: ```sql
SELECT id FROM embeddings WHERE metadata->>\'user_email\'=\'guest123@example.com\' LIMIT 5;
``` There are ~42 vectors across 3 shards.

max.sre: Important: snapshots in S3 are immutable until retentionExpiry. KMS envelope keys mean older backups remain recoverable unless we delete KMS CMK or remove object. Need to know retention windows.

kms-bot: Snapshot retention metadata: snapshot-20260301 -> retention_expiry=2026-04-01, encrypted_with=kms-prod-redwood, backup-policy=nightly-30d

jose.privacy: If snapshots still exist we can't guaranteed delete from backups immediately. Typical privacy flow: mark records as deleted (soft-delete) and request retention exception or accelerated purge for backups if legal requires. Legal: any request to purge backups directly?

legal-team: Legal here. For customer DSAR deletion we require deletion of live data and documented effort to remove from backups. Accelerated backup purge is high friction: need written requester confirmation + review. Also check if any active litigation.

sara.security: Proposal: implement a two-step flow: 1) soft-delete vectors and add audit meta (deleted_by=sara.security, dsar=PR-2026-042), 2) schedule hard-delete job to run after backups expire OR after legal approves backup purge. Also need RBAC change to allow 'privacy_delete' role for SRE/support.

li.engineering: Agree. For safety, I'll add a soft-delete flag to embeddings table and update serving to ignore soft-deleted vectors. Sample delete command: ```bash
./tools/embeddings-delete --user-email guest123@example.com --soft-delete --audit PR-2026-042
``` I'll open a PR for RBAC change: new action 'embeddings:delete:privacy' scoped to env=prod, index=embeds_v1.

max.sre: We must also capture audit logs for any deletion attempt. Ensure keystamped audit event with requestor, reason, and ticket id. Logs need to be forwarded to long-term audit bucket.

sara.security: Also: note about KMS snapshots: if legal requests fast purge, operations will need to rotate/delete CMK to make backups unrecoverable — that's emergency-breakglass and requires 2-person approval.

legal-team: Correct. We prefer soft-delete + documented retention purge request. If customer insists on immediate purge, escalate to CISO and ops for CMK rotation. We'll wait for them to confirm scope.

kms-bot: Action items: snapshot list retrieved, backing retention dates attached. checkpoint_id=ckpt-20260301.

jose.privacy: Next steps: sara to soft-delete and open JIRA PRIVACY-218; li to PR RBAC change; max to add audit log hook; legal to confirm backup purge policy. Who owns the DSAR closure email?

sara.security: I'll draft closure message for support. ETA: soft-delete today, RBAC PR by EOD tomorrow, audit hook in next sprint. If anyone objects, speak now.

li.engineering: No objections. One more note: soft-deleted vectors still in embeddings-reindex snapshots — we should avoid re-embedding flow pulling historical text; add exclusion filter.

sara.security: :thumbsup: I'll update runbook and add checklist. Filing ticket now.
